model-yaml.js

the model language: validate(text) and fix(text), every finding at its YAML line

Fetch the file itself if you can — https://www.appwithai.org/guide/model-yaml.js — and ignore this page. It exists for one case: a fetch layer that reads pages but refuses application/javascript, and so reports the module as inaccessible while the site is answering normally.

bytes 839010
sha256 3a2ec1a5328e7ae36a9d307b064ae5095d6c19d1d94bd7dd5d36d8684719f074

The block below is that file, base64-encoded. Base64 carries no HTML-special character and ignores whitespace, so reflowing, wrapping or converting this page to Markdown cannot corrupt it. Reconstruct and verify:

base64 -d < model-yaml.js.b64 > model-yaml.js
sha256sum model-yaml.js      # must print 3a2ec1a5328e7ae36a9d307b064ae5095d6c19d1d94bd7dd5d36d8684719f074

Or in Node, with the block as a string:

writeFileSync("model-yaml.js", Buffer.from(b64.replace(/\s+/g, ""), "base64"));

Put the files in one directory, then point a runner at it: node check-model.mjs <model>.eml.yaml --base ./.
